feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.08 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 m, kp 1.35) is the best design at 58.5, and every run still ends off_track with max_error at the 0.06 m floor. Iteration 5 showed that wheel_radius 0.04 m with scaled gains dropped the score to 41.4, with s-bend progress falling from 0.185 to 0.0625 and control effort staying high. So speed is not the lever, and I have reverted it. Iteration 2 (lighter body, mass 0.6 kg, y=0.07) lost s-bend progress from 0.163 to 0.119. That result is confounded, but it points toward added inertia helping stability, which is what this mass test checks. I kept the controller at iteration 4 values so the race reads the mass change alone. When the race reports: if s-bend progress holds at or above 0.185 and max_error or steering_oscillation falls, mass is helping, so keep 1.0 kg and test body_length next. If progress falls or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, extra mass is slowing the turn response, so go back to 0.8 kg and try a smaller wheel radius.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress holds at or above 0.185 and max_error or steering_oscillation falls: keep mass at 1.0 kg and raise body_length from 0.18 m to 0.22 m to add yaw inertia further without changing the off-track limit. Evidence: iteration 2 cut body_length and mass together and lost s-bend progress (0.163 to 0.119), so inertia appears to help.

If s-bend progress falls below 0.185 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2: return mass to 0.8 kg and try wheel_radius 0.025 m with wheel_track 0.08 m. Evidence: iteration 5 (wheel_radius 0.04 m) cut s-bend progress to 0.0625, so a smaller radius is the opposite direction to test.

Do not move the sensors to y=0.07 m, return wheel_track to 0.12 m, or raise wheel_radius above 0.03 m. Evidence: iteration 2 (y=0.07 with a lighter body) scored 47.8, iteration 1 (wheel_track 0.12 m) scored 55.1, and iteration 5 (wheel_radius 0.04 m) scored 41.4.
